Can drones and AI make farmers more money?

AgTech Amplified: Doug Houser of Iowa State University Extension joins the show to break down how farmers can put drones and AI to work.

Chris Torres,Editor,American AgriculturistNovember 6, 2026

link

Subscribe to Farm Progress AGTech — our free, twice-weekly newsletter delivering the latest innovations, emerging technologies and expert insights to your inbox.

Drones and AI. Oh my!

These new technologies have taken agriculture by storm. But how can tools like these help farmers be more efficient and make money?

In this episode of “AgTech Amplified” on the podcast “Farm Progress Nation,” Chris Torres, editor of American Agriculturist, and Andy Castillo, technology and equipment editor, take a deep dive into drones and artificial intelligence with guest Doug Houser of Iowa State University Extension.

Houser talks about the impacts of drones and AI; how farmers should think about adapting these technologies on the farm; and why autonomous drones are close to becoming a reality.

“The companies are working on it,” he said. “They have the capabilities to do it. I think it’s going to be here faster than we think.”

Related:What’s new in ag equipment? Key takeaways from fall shows

Houser worked for 30 years at Pioneer Seed before coming to Iowa State University Extension. He works in the university’s digital ag innovation lab.

Check out "Farm Progress Nation" every Friday and find it on YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts and other major podcast platforms.

About the Author

Chris Torres

Editor, American Agriculturist

Chris Torres, editor of American Agriculturist, previously worked at Lancaster Farming, where he started in 2006 as a staff writer and later became regional editor. Torres is a seven-time winner of the Keystone Press Awards, handed out by the Pennsylvania Press Association, and he is a Pennsylvania State University graduate.

Torres says he wants American Agriculturist to be farmers' "go-to product, continuing the legacy and high standard (former American Agriculturist editor) John Vogel has set." Torres succeeds Vogel, who retired after 47 years with Farm Progress and its related publications.

"The news business is a challenging job," Torres says. "It makes you think outside your small box, and you have to formulate what the reader wants to see from the overall product. It's rewarding to see a nice product in the end."

Torres' family is based in Lebanon County, Pa. His wife grew up on a small farm in Berks County, Pa., where they raised corn, soybeans, feeder cattle and more. Torres and his wife are parents to three young boys.

无人机和人工智能。天哪！

这些新技术已经席卷了农业领域。但像这样的工具如何帮助农民提高效率并赚钱呢？

在播客“Farm Progress Nation”的“AgTech Amplified”本期节目中，《American Agriculturist》编辑Chris Torres和技术与设备编辑Andy Castillo与爱荷华州立大学推广部的嘉宾Doug Houser一起深入探讨了无人机和人工智能。

Houser谈到了无人机和人工智能的影响；农民应如何考虑在农场中采用这些技术；以及为什么自主无人机即将成为现实。

“公司正在努力研发，”他说。“他们有能力做到。我认为它会比我们想象的更快到来。”

Houser在来到爱荷华州立大学推广部之前，曾在Pioneer Seed工作了30年。他在该大学的数字农业创新实验室工作。

每周五收看“Farm Progress Nation”，可在YouTube、Spotify、Apple Podcasts和其他主要播客平台上找到。
